pairs: Et factum est in quartodecimo anno regis Ezechiæ,
And it happened that, in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah,
Sennacherib, the king of the Assyrians,
went up against all the fortified cities of Judah,
Et misit rex Assyriorum Rabsacen de Lachis in Jerusalem,
And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabshakeh from Lachish into Jerusalem,
ad regem Ezechiam in manu gravi:
to king Hezekiah, with a great force,
et stetit in aquæductu piscinæ superioris in via Agri fullonis.
and he stood near the aqueduct of the upper pool, at the road to the fuller’s field.
Et egressus est ad eum Eliacim,
And those who went to him were Eliakim,
Quæ est ista fiducia qua confidis?
What is this faith in which you believe?
aut quo consilio vel fortitudine rebellare disponis?
And by what counsel or strength would you prepare to rebel?
In whom do you have faith,
so much so that you would withdraw from me?
Ecce confidis super baculum arundineum confractum istum,
in that broken staff of a reed.
But if a man were to lean against it,
it would enter his hand and pierce it.
to all who trust in him.
But if you answer me by saying:
‘We trust in the Lord our God.’
nonne ipse est cujus abstulit Ezechias excelsa et altaria,
Is it not his high places and altars that Hezekiah has taken away?
And he has said to Judah and to Jerusalem,
Et nunc trade te domino meo,
And now, hand yourselves over to my lord,
et dabo tibi duo millia equorum,
and I will give you two thousand horses,
nec poteris ex te præbere ascensores eorum:
and you will not be able to find riders for them on your own.
et quomodo sustinebis faciem judicis unius loci ex servis domini mei minoribus?
So how will you withstand the face of the ruler of even one place,
of even the least of my lord’s subordinates?
But if you trust in Egypt,
in four-horse chariots and in horsemen:
et nunc numquid sine Domino ascendi ad terram istam, ut disperderem eam?
do I intend to go up against this land to destroy it without the Lord?
But the Lord said to me,
Loquere ad servos tuos syra lingua;
“Speak to your servants in the Syrian language.
ne loquaris ad nos judaice in auribus populi qui est super murum.
Do not speak to us in the Jewish language, in the hearing of the people, who are upon the wall.”
Numquid ad dominum tuum et ad te misit me dominus meus,
“Has my lord sent me to your lord
and to you in order to speak all these words,
et non potius ad viros qui sedent in muro,
and not even more so to the men who are sitting on the wall,
so that they may eat their own dung
et bibant urinam pedum suorum vobiscum?
and drink their own urine with you?”
and he cried out with a loud voice in the Jewish language,
“Listen to the words of the great king,
Do not let Hezekiah deceive you.
For he will not be able to rescue you.
Et non vobis tribuat fiduciam Ezechias super Domino,
And do not let Hezekiah cause you to trust in the Lord,
‘The Lord will rescue and free us.
non dabitur civitas ista in manu regis Assyriorum.
This city will not be given into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.’
For the king of the Assyrians says this:
Act with me to your own benefit,
And let each one eat from his own vine,
and each one from his own fig tree.
et bibite unusquisque aquam cisternæ suæ,
And let each one drink water from his own well,
donec veniam, et tollam vos ad terram quæ est ut terra vestra,
until I arrive and take you away to a land which is like your own:
a land of grain and of wine,
a land of bread and of vineyards.
But you should not let Hezekiah disturb you,
Numquid liberaverunt dii gentium unusquisque terram suam de manu regis Assyriorum?
Have any of the gods of each of the nations delivered their land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
Ubi est deus Emath et Arphad?
Where is the god of Hamath and of Arpad?
Where is the god of Sepharvaim?
numquid liberaverunt Samariam de manu mea?
Have they freed Samaria from my hand?
Quis est ex omnibus diis terrarum istarum qui eruerit terram suam de manu mea,
Who is there, among all the gods of these lands, who has rescued his land from my hand,
ut eruat Dominus Jerusalem de manu mea?
so that the Lord would rescue Jerusalem from my hand?”
and did not answer a word to him.
For the king had commanded them,
filius Helciæ, qui erat super domum,
who was over the house, and Shebna,
a commentariis, ad Ezechiam, scissis vestibus,
entered to Hezekiah with their garments rent,
and they reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
